newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end lower, technical rebound seen.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end lower, technical rebound seen.

text.p: Shrugging off a rally on Wall Street, Chilean blue chips sank to a year-low on Tuesday, traders said.
The decline raised the possibility of a technical rebound at the opening of the next session, they said.
"There could be a technical rally, but we see little sign of any fundamental change in the market," said Pablo Salcedo, head of research of ING Barings.
The selective IPSA index ended 0.82 percent lower at a year-low of 88.02 points. The general IGPA index shed 0.59 percent to 4,877 points on volume of 14.7 billion pesos.
Traders said the market was searching for a new support level which could be as low as 85 points.

The market reacted positively to news that a consortium including telecoms company CTC won an auction for a 35 percent stake in Brazilian telephone firm CRT with a bid of 681 million reais, said traders.
"It was good news, but the rise in CTC stock price was a trading reaction as the impact on the company's earnings is not significant," said one dealer.
CTC, which is a minority partner in the consortium, ended up 0.56 percent at 2,350 pesos.
Decliners included financial group Cruz Blanca after news that a Chilean group will pay about $75 million for 51 percent of the firm's insurance unit, traders said.
Cruz Blanca had originally said that the group had offered $200 million for the whole division, they said.
Cruz Blanca tumbled 6.76 percent to 138 pesos.
Other decliners included telecoms company Telex, down 5.05 percent to 940 pesos, and power utility Endesa, which shed 1.45 percent to 214-1/4 pesos.
